convention: git_blob_sha1 is `git hash-object` for the exact bytes staged, so it identifies the content the commit carries; committed_blob_sha1 is what HEAD actually holds, and the two agree for every implementation path in this report. A commit cannot contain its own id, so the report of a commit is carried by the commit that follows it, and the id is returned in the mission's final response (CURRENT_HEAD).

the due rule is 'this slot has no window yet', which the 84-window plan does not bound: a tick between 2026-10-22T16:00Z and the close would attempt an undeclared 85th window. Measured, declared, not patched: patching the collection rule mid-period would change the campaign.
--authorize-extension can neither extend the period nor leave collection alone during it; the safe behaviour (never extend) is what runs.
